I'm very annoyed since this stuff is very simple when one can work within RTM concepts as framework for trading. My minds overcomplicates everything I do... from errands to run - to day job, same applies to trading. I see some guys here in RTM using very very simplistic approach though it is very elegant in terms how they trade and what they achieve.

Seems mind is the greatest obstacle. It just complicates simple things. It is overwhelming and tiring.

Just by looking at someone's chart you can in seconds spot how good they are. If charts are simple and all relevant information is marked - dude/gal knows what they are doing. If there is shitloads if clutter - chances are they are lost. After looking back through my charts, not matter how sad it looks, it is obvious that charts are messy.. too much clutter.

A marked chart is the best indication of one's market understanding. Probably not the trading's skill though..

Another thing to note... I get lost if I have too many instruments on the platform. My mind is not ready to follow 10 different instruments and run analysis on each of them with great detail.
@Aswilled, kudos man on your last trade;-)

Another confusion area is timing to initiate the trade. Very often price reaches SD... is rejected once, twice and sometimes even 3rd time. Last rejection when it moves with velocity is the optimal trade. The first waves from the SD are plausible trades/scalps IMO.

This has been bugging me for a while now. I find he areas but timing is just so wrong.

The best thing place to start looking into this is IF's last UJ trade

Supply Anatomy. Seems the key level was the DP for the big drop.

So this was the first example of ¨Timing¨ series. If price reached a SD areas and is rejected and even if FL/low is engulfed does not mean it is ready for a decent trade.
